tips.comment:
This horse won well at Doncaster last time out when battling to a hard earned victory.
Carries a penalty here and can win this before being raised in class.
Gnomon has been running in class 1 and 2 races and not disgracing himself. He has won a bumper and can go well on soft. Today's rain forecast should suit him above some of the other runners.

The Bellhop looks a strong value bet stepping back into a race that should suit both tactically and on ability. He's been shaping better than the form suggests, after missing the break and not really getting a clear chance last time out. With a clearer run and slightly more pace to aim at, he's more than capable of getting involved. Lingfield's configuration suits his style, and he's run decently in similar conditions before. I think he's overpriced and underestimated today.

Disappointed on debut at Nottingham in October when failing to beat a single rival. Should be better than that result showed and likely to improve having been gelded and having joined a new yard. Any improvement gives an each-way chance.
Having just been touched off last week at Yarmouth, comes here seeking compensation. Sire Mayson has a decent record with horses making a quick turnaround.

Four runs on the AW this year for the 6yo, and four close defeats. A 4 month break will do him no harm going off his previous form. He was rated 13lb higher at one point just over a year ago. A bit of give in the ground is another positive. He looks good EW value with bet365 offering 3 places for this 7 runner handicap.

Can do much better than LTO effort when only 6 of 7 at Wolverhampton back in April of this year. Need him to get back to the kind of form that saw him win here also in April of this year. Dropped mark might help.
Had a day to forget at Newmarket when 9 of 9 last month. In truth, he can do much better and does have bags of ability, as evident when achieving 3 consecutive wins last year.

Gelded son of Advertise & Mother Love ( Dam's sire Heeraat ) who was last seen at Thirsk 7 days ago where gaining his second career success out of three handicap starts and arrives here racing on an unchanged mark of 68 leaving R Spencer's inmate poised to strike yet again having escaped a penalty for that success he should take good advantage of his current operating mark and should be taken very seriously here as this an excellent opportunity to catch him winning again before the handicapper applies pressure steps up in trip racing at the 1 mile 1 furlong trip here for the first time that being a good move by his connections as this new trip can bring out even further improvement from this individual jockey Jack Callan takes off a very valuable looking 7lb which only enhances his good looking claims here and can steer Atmosphere to victory yet again bold showing is anticipated here

Post Rider is trained by Oliver Cole, who has a win, which was by 3.25 lengths at 14/1 and ridden by William Buick, and a 2nd from his two horses since starting off on his own. Oliver has an excellent record at Lingfield when in partnership with his father, so he may have chosen a good course to continue his good form. Post Rider has only been out of the places twice, and they were on the all-weather at the beginning of his career. He has won after a layoff of 150 days and followed that up with a win over 8.5f. He has a record of two wins and three places from his five turf runs, and the booking of Oisin Murphy is quite significant for such a new trainer.
Second last time, beaten favorite, good jockey and trainer, back up in distance should do the trick. Should be given serious consideration, a great each-way shot at 7/1, Nap Each Way.

Just four career runs for the 3yo, form 33-42. A runner-up two weeks ago, which was his turf and handicap debut that day. The form looks strong. Same mark for this handicap and every chance there is more improvement in him.
Blenheim Star last won in April off a 64, with all runs this year being on GF, but did get a win last year on soft. Today's mark is just 1 lb above that last winning mark EW.

Marsh Benham is a 6-year-old gelding trained by George Baker. He has 7 wins out of 41 on turf, winning off handicap marks ranging between 62-68 (three-time winner off 68), so he sits just 1 lb higher on 69 under Pat Cosgrave, who has 113 wins out of 899 for George Baker, showing an impressive profit of £129.00. Marsh Benham is also ground versatile, winning on various ground conditions ranging from heavy to good to firm. Baker also landed an 18-1 winner with his penultimate runner, Beauld As Brass, and his yard could be just hitting a purple patch. Only concern is the trip but all in all there are a lot of positives.
Roman Emperor won well last time at Yarmouth last month and could be on a good handicap mark here in conditions that will suit.

Won over 7 furlongs on penultimate start and third of six beat half a length over that same trip here last time out. Ridden by today's jockey in both of those races and likely to be on the premises again dropping in trip and is twice a previous winner over this trip on all-weather tracks.

Taking a chance on the Jim and Suzi Best runner, Comedian Leader, who has been running well at Brighton. If he brings his best form here today at Lingfield, he should certainly be capable of being involved in the finish.

Not been at her best in a couple of runs this season since she had a wind operation, but soft ground is fine. Her mark is well below all five of her wins, and she has a win over this C&D in the past, so she has enough boxes ticked at a huge price to take a chance.

Both trainer and jockey are going through a good patch of wins at present. The good-to-soft predicted conditions should suit this horse. Placed here on the poly track with the same rider in January and has had two runs back off a 139-day let-up, so you'd expect some benefit to now be coming through with those runs under the belt. Improved effort at Brighton and that could be the indicator to a big odds upset (he said hopefully).

Miss Collada is a 3-year-old filly trained by Richard Hannon. He has run in stronger races than this in 2025 and is on a good mark now on 72, particularly after a 2.25-length defeat at Newmarket on his penultimate start over 6f, posting a RPR of 77. He finished 4th out of 22 at York four starts back in a class 4 handicap. Not so good over 7f at Epsom last start, but connections may have discovered that todays 6f is probaly hee best trip in a weaker-looking contest having won twice over 5f as a 2-year-old, once in a class 4 at Salisbury on today's good ground, and winning a class 4 over 7f on the AW.

Three career starts for the 3yo filly. Back from an 8 month break recently with a nice 2L maiden win on the AW, a decent yardstick in second, the 3rd was beaten 7L. She’s making her turf and handicap debut in this contest but her opening mark of 72 looks attractive. Strong jockey booking.
Ran her best race to date when runner-up over course and distance last time. She is eased in grade here, nudged up a pound for that decent effort, and has a strong each-way chance.

Spiritualism won when first up after wind surgery off a 68 last month. While I always expect more when second up after wind surgery, her last win was on the AW off a 70 in October. So, I think there is more to come today.

A thin looking class 6 handicap here with my vote going to Spirit Star a daughter of Territories & Star Girl ( Dam's sire Dutch Art ) who was last seen at Yarmouth 13 days ago where finishing 4th/5 however she did shape better than that bare result suggests in my point of view currently operating on a mark of 46 M Botti's inmate is very well likely to be much better than that heading down the handicap route in very good time and is open to plenty of progress at this stage and having found herself a straightforward assignment that shouldn't take much winning here Spirit Star can get off the mark here and possesses all the necessary credentials to take a race of this nature jockey Benoit D L Sayette takes the ride and can give Spirit Star a promising ride here at Lingfield must be considered in a race of this nature
Supernova Steps has been looking in excellent form lately and should be up to winning this, given the quality of the opposition.
Ran a good race last time out when 3rd at this course 31 days ago and looks open to improvement. Well backed and cheekpieces back on.
Spirit Charmer has not won yet! It has run a couple of promising races off a mark of 50. Now into a classified race on a mark of 44 with Oisin Murphy on top. Worth an E/W bet!
Currently not in the best of form, but it does help that the last handicap win was off a higher mark and also has experience over C&D, which might come in handy.

A chance is taken here on Proud Nation to win on debut. He must have impressed in the breeze-up to have been bought for 320,000. The field of newcomers doesn't look all that exciting, and Yy Nation was poor in his race at York. Although he is likely to come on from that, I think Proud Nation is more likely to be the answer to this race here.
Has been disappointing in both races to date. Should be better than those runs have shown, and with improvement likely to come at some stage, holds an each-way chance.
Looks the one to beat here after a brace of seconds at Catterick over 5f and 6f, so distance shouldn't be a problem. Those races were also in the same class as this one.

Made All won with a bit in hand at Catterick last week, and looks a likely winner in this modest handicap. He does have to overcome a five pound penalty for that win, however the very useful Cian Horgan claims five which is a big help. The trainer is in good form, and can continue her run here.

Jim Goldie (SR 24%) is in good form right now. Since moving up to staying trips, Ana Emaraaty has won three races in succession on the all-weather and has been staying on well at the close of his races on turf. Ran third in an apprentice handicap a week ago and comes here in good form. Paul Mulrennan replaces the apprentice from last time. The five-year-old looks a contender at this weak (0-58) level.

Lightly raced 4yo. Four runs this year, all on the AW, shaping a little better four weeks ago when only tiring very late on. A return to turf is fine. He was a close runner-up last summer, splitting two smart rivals who are both rated 77 and 98 now. The selection has a 10lb lower mark now, racing off a 57 mark and dropping into a class 6 handicap.

Yes, the form is not inspiring with three 8th placings since resuming from a long spell but has needed them and hasn't done himself any favours by racing keenly in front in two of them and missing the jump in the other one. Why they continue to lead on him is beyond me, but I'm hoping they revert to racing him in behind as he placed third on debut when those tactics were adopted.

Not many shortlist in this one, so MAX THE TIGER is one that could get involved at a big price. Second and third favorites Rory The Cat and Ana Emaraaty have questions over the break and the performance on turf, so there's a chance one of these outsiders comes close to Made All. He's obviously the clear favorite, but in class six racing, you never know; that form could drop.

Won over the distance last time out at Thirsk. Up six pounds for that win, still looks well treated today. Plenty of pace in the race for him. Ground conditions today will suit. Stable going well. Should be hard to beat today.

Our Absent Friends has been kindly dropped a couple of pounds for finishing third last week, which is a little surprising given that wasn't a bad effort. He has form in better class races than this, including here at Musselburgh, and shouldn't be far away.

Miss Brazen is in good form and, despite being hiked 8lb for a win and runner-up effort, has a strong chance of winning this. Recent form has worked well and finished 2nd here on sole course visit when trained by Karl Burke. Gets the highest stall draw, which is preferred here at Musselburgh, especially over 5f.

Everything this trainer touches at the moment turns to gold, and this one looks a cracking e/w bet at 8/1 to finish in the first 3. The horse has arguably been racing on ground that's too lively for much of the season, but he looks a better horse on ground just the softer side of good. Mulrennan is booked for just the 2nd time, and despite going up the handicap recently, the horse is still well handicapped on some of his 2yo form. His maiden win from Educating Rita, for example, would suggest that he's well capable of winning off this mark with seemingly his ideal conditions here.

Won over this trip on soft ground at Nottingham in October 2024 off a mark of 73 and races off 68 here. He has also won over this trip on good to firm so is ground versatile and looks to be on a tempting mark.
Comes here at the lowest mark. Had a good run here recently, finishing a respectable 4th. First time ride for jockey who tends to ride very well at this course. Each way play here.

Good Point has shown signs of ability, he was hit with a fairly harsh rating at the start of his career. A little unruly on return to this course last time. This looks a good opportunity to get down to business and show some of his earlier form when some of his better runs came when having to deal with tough conditions.

Beaten favorite last time at Doncaster when running on very late, meeting plenty of interference. Drops in the handicap again and down in class again. Trainer Karl Burke has a great strike rate at Musselburgh of 28% and has his horses in good form. He only sends 2 to the course today.
She is looking for 3 in a row here and could easily complete today. Loves this track, and Allen retains the ride for this one.

Two turf runs this year for the 4yo. He was nice winner three weeks ago over this 7f trip, still well back turning into the straight but stayed on strong, winning the 9 runner contest a shade cosy in the end by 1 1/2L. He can take another step forward and a 3lb higher mark might not stop him.

Shaped encouragingly on handicap debut last time and comes here off the same mark in a similar race. Did well in the circumstances last time, having been poorly placed and conceded first run as a result, doing well to finish 2nd.

Elvetham is a 3-year-old gelding making a stable debut for Michael Bell and runs off a lowly 48 with Jay Mackay taking off 5lb. He has run well in two big field handicaps at Naas and Leopardstown the last twice. He finished a neck behind Tartaraghan at Leopardstown when finishing 6/16, and Tartaraghan won on the next start and is now rated 8lb higher. Today's task is nowhere near as difficult or competitive, and Elvetham, previously in good hands with D K Weld, looks likely to go close in making a winning UK debut.
Course winner here. Drops another 3lb with claimer on board. Finished neck at this distance, now 10lb lower with claimer on board.

Looks well treated back on the flat after making all to win a handicap hurdle at Perth LTO, the same race he won last year, and the 2nd has come out to frank the form. Ran well here on the level back in April in a class 4 when 4th behind Sportingsilvermine over 12f. 1lb lower here and back up in trip in a lesser grade.
A course winner that is one of the steamers of the day, unlucky in running last time out and capable of far better form than shown.

This G Boughey-trained 2-year-old gelding has finished second in three of his last four races. The latest was over five furlongs on good to firm ground at Thirsk seven days ago, when only beaten a short head behind the K R Burke-trained Dinamo. So with Billy Loughnane doing the steering, he looks hard to oppose.

Interesting contest where the value appears to be the outsider of the party, Carefree Dream, who has shaped better than bare result in a pair of decent 6f Chepstow novice/maidens, giving the impression a drop to 5f could spark improvement. Easy to forgive effort last time out and switch to 5f here likely to suit much better. Looks overpriced at 10/1 and good value.
3 of 5 flat wins have been over this course and distance, with the last of those wins being off a 7lb higher mark. Likely to be there or thereabouts.

Arch Legend is a 4-time winner trained by Ruth Carr. He is a course winner for previous trainer Mark Johnston off a mark of 61 under Franny Norton (no claim) and runs off 46 today with Miss Charli Parker and her 5lb claim. He showed signs of a revival at Doncaster last time out under Miss Charli Parker off 48 (5lb claim): 'Prominent early, soon led, headed over 3f out, lost second over 1f out, soon hung left and weakened, beaten 5.5l.' So, 2lb lower today over 1/2f shorter and a return back to the AW the scene of his only victory on the AW could see Arch Legend in a better light!
Twice a winner on the all-weather, with the latest of those wins being here last September. May need the run, having not been seen since October, but holds an each-way chance.

Lyra Lea was running steadily on debut when running green. Then, when the penny dropped, he finished strongly. With normal improvement, Lewis Edmunds should steer him home at the Wolverhampton evening meeting.

She made her debut over 6f at Newbury in June and was only beaten a couple of lengths in finishing 3rd. There were clear signs of inexperience then, but she made some improvement last time over the same course and distance when finishing 3rd. More to come and is interesting switched to the AW.
Honeyforthebears was mainly in the rear on debut a couple of weeks ago in a C4 and a distant fourth, but will come on for that run with a drop to C5 today. Likely to show improvement EW.

After winning and being second twice in Class 6, SOUTH DAKOTA SIOUX found Class 5 a stretch last time (although not being completely outclassed) but will surely go well returning to this lower class and off the same mark (62) as when only beaten a length at this venue.

Master Dandy looks poised to go close here after shaping with more promise than the form book suggests. He's now returning to Wolverhampton, a track where his run style can be more effective, especially in a race that lacks depth and pace pressure. With a strong mid-race move and a significant jockey booking, he has the skills to outstay this field late on.

In poor form the last 2 starts, which is a stark contrast to an impressive win at Wolverhampton last September. Now operating 4lbs higher than the last winning mark, and 2 of the last 4 runs have been at this course.
Penelope Valentine has only had one win so far at Kempton in a C6 off a 59 back in February by nearly 5L. It has taken until now to drop back to that last winning mark and is worth a shot.

Time After Time is a 3-year-old filly trained by Heather Main and owned and bred by Mr. & Mrs. D. R. Guest. She takes a drop in class after a promising run from 4lb out of the handicap at Goodwood last time out. 'Dwelt start, towards rear, outpaced 2f out, rallied final furlong, nearest finish (under today's jockey Jack Dace).' Time After Time is out of a dam, Medoras Childe, owned by Mr. & Mrs. D. R. Guest and bred by the Mains, who won at Kempton. Time After Time is a second foal and half-sister to Ash Wednesday, also bred and owned by Mr. & Mrs. D. R. Guest, who won six times on the AW in 2025, trained by Heather Main, rising in the handicap from 47-76, winning 4 times at Wolverhampton. Time After Time could have been found a good opportunity today in this class 6 and runs off a 3lb lower mark today as the handicapper has dropped her 1lb, and Jack Dace is able to claim his full allowance of 7lb (5lb last time). Heather Main also does well at Wolverhampton with 29 wins and a £53.67 profit.

At the top third of the handicap mark in this field and improved performance in only the second handicap run when 11th of 16 at Leicester back in May of this year. She has a chance if she can take advantage of the dropped mark.

Disappointed in 3 starts on turf last year and finished last of 7 on handicap debut 11 days ago despite being gelded. Should be better than results have shown and steps up in trip for handicap debut. Any improvement gives an each-way chance.

The model I run suggests Sunny South West can win this one. Sunny South West lines up here with a comparably high RPR but is not overly penalized for it in the weights. Steps out carrying a small amount more than the other runners in this smaller 6 horse field, but comes here with great form figures and looks to make it 3 wins on the spin. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which has been driven by the poor value on offer with these already short odds. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Gavin Cromwell trained 6yo I Am Mimi improved on maiden hurdle form to win on handicap hurdle debut 56 days ago here at Ballinrobe. It was a convincing effort, going easily 2 out, and going away at the finish. This is only a little classier in grade. Keith Donoghue returns for the ride. Contender.

The model I run suggests Artsncrafts can win this one. Artsncrafts lines up here with the highest RPR in a limited experience National Hunt Flat. A lot of other runners have not raced before, and experience can be key in races like this. Good second when last out and will look to make some more improvement to get over the line first here today. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator due to the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Tricksofthetrade managed to finish fourth on his bumper debut and looks sure to improve with that run. Could give the hot favorite plenty to think about here.

The horses that have run before don't look to be anything special, so this race could go to one of the well-bred newcomers. Gameball and Largy Meadow both fit the bill, and preference is for Gameball. He is by the high-quality National Hunt sire Yeats and out of a Flemensfirth mare who produced the high-class Maries Rock amongst others. His trainer, Andrew Slattery, has a good bumper record and is having a particularly good time with his bumper runners recently.
Has been running well in handicap company and has been runner-up on five occasions. Returning to maiden she looks sure to appreciate this drop in grade.

The model I run suggests Nothing Hectic can win this one. Nothing Hectic lines up here with the second highest RPR of the larger 15-runner field but has an official ranking that leaves him looking well treated in the weights. Steps out carrying the joint lowest weight around this 2m 1f round trip. Form figures point to some slow but steady improvement and maybe some more improvement in this race might be enough to get over the line first. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Ran his best race yet over hurdles at Cork last time when 5th in a big field novice over 17f. Didn’t get a hard ride and well worth considering before presumably going down the handicap route.
Given he didn't jump very well at all last time out, he did well to win, and the form has since been franked. Expect improved jumping here and the one to beat.
Drumgill is a twice-over course and distance winner who comes from the yard that turned out the winner of this race last year.

With Tiernan Power Roche claiming 5lbs, Mercury Mission may be the answer to this nine runner handicap hurdle. Paddy Rothwell yard has had a couple of recent winners. The 6yo, by Ulysses, scored two wins over hurdles back in March and April from ORs of 100 and 106. Ran respectably in a fiercer contest than this at Bellewstown recently (Summer Plate Chase winner Ballysax Hank was third). Could prove one of the better handicapped of these.

The model I run suggests The Mediator can win this one. The Mediator lines up here with the highest RPR of this 9-horse field but has an official ranking that leaves him middle order. This subsequently means The Mediator steps out with 7 lbs less to carry than the current market favorite. The Mediator is also a prior distance winner, so knows how to get it done at this trip. The model has issued a 'very low' indicator, which has been driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

If Bhean Saibhre runs two days in a row, she has another chance to break her maiden tag, this time over hurdles, after being a beaten favorite yesterday, just failing to get up by half a length off her basement mark of 42 on the flat. However, over hurdles, she has also been close to winning. Last time, she was asserting again in the lead when unseating two out at Roscommon and was 2nd previously at Clonmel.

Having made the frame in his three starts in bumpers and having switched to hurdling, he has run two promising races at Downpatrick, both over 19f. There should be more to come, and he looks a strong player.

The model I run suggests No More Silver can win this one. No More Silver lines up here with a comparably high RPR to the other runners but is not penalized for it in the weights. Steps out carrying the second lowest amount of weight in this larger 14 horse field. Decent 4th when last out only 11 days ago and turned around in short order to try and capitalize on some form and improvement. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator due to the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Where Are You Now is a 4-year-old gelding trained by E Bolger and owned by J P McManus. He finished 8/22 on his hurdles debut at Punchestown, finishing 39.75 lengths behind but met trouble in running, getting badly hampered at the fourth flight after fiddling the second flight. So, not the most auspicious of starts to his hurdles career. He is related to two winners bred by Noreen McManus and owned by J P McManus and trained by E Bolger. Bolger will know the intricacies associated with Where Are You Now's training. Being out of a dam called Upsie (Willie Mullins), brought over from France and bought by J P McManus after winning two bumpers, he was rated as high as 147 after starting his career winning three successive wins for Mullins. If today is not the day, Where Are You Now will probably have a bright future.

4-year-old dual-purpose type who has 1 win and 3 placed efforts from 13 career runs over both codes. The win came back in April at Bellewstown over today's 17f trip off a mark of 107. Has run 3 times since, 2 runs back at Leopardstown over 9f, and last run 17 days ago again at Bellewstown over today's 17f trip when coming 6th of 16 off a mark of 111, which stays at today. Tip is the only N. Meade runner on the card. He's saddled 5 winners from 17 hurdlers saddled over the last 3 years with a +LSP of €36.38.

Mark Walsh rode Realism on a few occasions for former yard of Joseph O'Brien and is booked for first start for trainer Enda Bolger (SR 25%). Connections strongly respected and Realism has been given a lengthy break ahead of first start for the new yard. This six year-old by Galileo has run well at times (third in a Group 3 early on in career), has often gone close in handicap hurdle competition but remains a maiden. New stable commands respect.
Didn’t get the clearest of runs last time at Tipperary when in midfield over two miles. Steps up slightly in trip today from a 2lb lower mark and won’t be far away.

Only One Plan is only one pound above his last winning mark and looks interesting in this Ballinrobe handicap hurdle. He has two career wins, the last coming at Down Royal on September 24 off a mark of 95. Raised 5 lbs for that, he was unplaced in his next 5 starts but dropped back to 95 and finished second 11 days ago at Kilbeggan. He is raised 1 lb for that but still looks like a good each-way bet with 4 places on offer.

This horse is thoroughly unexposed, and the trainer has been trying all sorts of trips. The horse is dropped back from around 3 miles to around 2 here, and this trip looks much more suitable. The trainer's runners are going really well, and he's booked one of the stronger jockeys, which looks like a statement of intent. The horse has been dropped 2 lb after that debut handicap run over too far last time out, and he could well be much more competitive here.

The model I run suggests Stily can win this one. Stily lines up here with a comparably high RPR but an official ranking that leaves him ranked bottom. This means Stily steps out carrying the lowest initial weight of the 15 runner field. Tries the tongue tie for the first time to aid concentration and Sean O'Keeffe picks up the reins for this 2m 1f trial. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Has run to a similar level in three novice events without troubling the judge. Now moves into handicaps from a reasonable-looking mark and could improve significantly on what we’ve seen so far.

A wide-open handicap where Silent Dawn ran well for a long way last time out at Kilbeggan after a few months off. He should be fitter today, looks well-handicapped, and if he can repeat his solid 3rd at Clonmel a few runs back, he should be bang there.

Another big priced runner who I also think will benefit from dropping back in Trip is Maike Magnussen's 6 year old Mare DANIELLE D who didn't embarrass herself 36 days ago on handicap debut (at Kilbeggan) when running well but fading 3 from home, you might be thinking 'Ok then surely around the 20-21f mark would be suffice not 17f?' and yes you'd be correct BUT this Daughter of OCOVANGO's best run was a 5th place at Navan (16f keeping on) in April. A big plus is the booking of Jockey Johnny Shinnick who sheds 3lbs adding to the 3lb shaved off from the handicapper. Jockey also has a 40% ojsve strike rate here at Ballinrobe the past year. Cheekpieces are applied today, look at 40/1 this charge is a risky proposition in the fact that we don't know her best trip but it certainly does look like a step back is the way. Very small each way stakes.

A weak race and one that Kingkong Ciergues should win if taking to good ground. His last two efforts were more than respectable but came on soft or heavy ground. They're much better than anything else in this field has achieved recently.
With only one win from 32 starts, Nazine isn't the most consistent of runners, but its second place last time shows he's running into form.

Kalaroun is a 7-year-old gelding trained by Conor O'Dwyer. His official rating was hiked some 12 lb after finishing 2/6 on his penultimate start behind Avala, who won by 6 lengths over 2m 4f on good ground. Avala then finished 6/16 behind Gimme A Buzz, who was making it two wins in a row. The 3/6 Adaliz, who had won the previous race, won next time out, winning a 16-runner handicap hurdle at Tipperary, so solid form lines. Kalaroun has since disappointed in a Punchestown handicap hurdle on his next start. The handicapper has subsequently dropped Kalaroun back down to 87 from 95, so he could bounce back today off the current mark and down slightly in trip on what seems like preferred good ground.
Softer ground would be a help but she has dropped to a very tempting mark these days and the first-time cheekpieces that she sports could be a good way to find her best form again.

Scottish Dancer came into good form in its last four runs of last season with two seconds, a third, and a win. It's ten months since its last race, but if he can get over the long layoff, he has a chance.
I thought that Lariat was perhaps a shade unlucky when getting a squeezed out sixth on the flat last time out. A similar effort here should see him go close.

The Sydney Cruiser lines up here with the highest RPR of the 16-runner field but has an official ranking that leaves him very well treated off this mark. Steps out carrying the second lowest weight over this slightly longer 2m 6f trip. Alex Harvey on board relieves a further 5 lbs, which is helpful on the slightly longer distance. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Placed over C&D from this mark in May 2024, winning at Downpatrick over this trip in August. The distance was too short on her return to action, but she could strip fitter now, returned to a more suitable trip.

Davy Fitzgerald's 6 year old Gelding ISTHEREONEMOREINME is a massive price here currently trading at 40/1 deservedly so this Son of OCOVANGO hasn't shown much in his 2 handicap endeavours so far BUT I thought this charge ran well for a long way 36 days ago at Kilbeggan (24f Good) keeping in touch with the main players before fading 2 from home. This lad now drops 2f aswell as 3lbs & gets another 3lbs from Jockey Gavin Brouder. Trainer has a 40% place strike rate the past month. With 5 places on offer should this lad run similarly than he did for his career best last time out then on the evidence he 'could' be bang there over this shorter trip at big odds.
